bib.title: Pyserini: A Python Toolkit for Reproducible Information Retrieval Research with Sparse and Dense Representations
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference (SIGIR '21), Resource Paper

question: Can one pip-installable Python toolkit provide reproducible first-stage retrieval (sparse, dense and hybrid) for research on multi-stage neural ranking?
contributions: Pyserini: Python interface to Anserini/Lucene with Faiss dense and hybrid retrieval
Bundled queries, qrels, pre-built indexes and evaluation scripts for ~three dozen test collections
Access to postings, document vectors and term statistics
Reproducible baselines on MS MARCO passage and document ranking

method.summary: Toolkit paper. Sparse BM25 via Lucene/Anserini, dense via Faiss (brute-force or HNSW) with existing encoders (TCT-ColBERT, DPR, ANCE, DistilBERT KD), hybrid via weighted interpolation of sparse and dense scores. Baselines reported on MS MARCO passage and document leaderboards.
method.task: first-stage retrieval (MS MARCO passage and document ranking)

limits: Interpolation weight and HNSW settings are not given; no latency is reported.
BM25 parameters tuned on a subset of dev queries that are also used for reporting dev scores.
Evaluated on MS MARCO only; document-task dense retrieval is zero-shot.
Dense support less mature than sparse; no representation learning in scope.
Reproducibility discussion and future plans deferred to an arXiv extended version.
Hardware and query throughput not reported.

terms.definition: bag-of-words ranking with BM25; the authors note this naming is not common parlance
each document segmented into passages indexed separately; document score is max of passage scores
